ticket.description:
# KS-1153 R-918-A: pin run-code-guards.sh's `--check-unreached` advisory-skip arm (a non-git tree skips the census, rc 0)

File: `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/run_code_guards.test.sh`
Tip: `52df64f844b7b3aabf7df57284c5f4e2ab8a07a2`

KS-1153's first "Done when" item: "R-918-A: one cell pins the advisory-skip arm (a non-git tree -> `SKIP (advisory)` line
+ rc 0)". The arm is `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/run-code-guards.sh:145-148` at develop `52df64f84`, and no cell of
`run_code_guards.test.sh` reaches it: every fixture there is a real `git init` tree. This adds CASE 9, a fixture that is
NOT a git checkout (the runner copied into a plain directory, git's upward search stopped at the suite's own temp dir),
and two cells through the suite's own `check` helper. Test-only: the product script is never edited.

## The exact change

```diff
@@ -156,1 +156,10 @@
+echo "=== CASE 9 - ADVISORY SKIP: a tree that is NOT a git checkout skips the census with rc 0 (KS-1153 R-918-A) ==="
+# Preflight leg 15 runs --check-unreached. From an export with no .git the census cannot enumerate tracked guards; it
+# must say so and step aside with rc 0 (run-code-guards.sh:145-148). Every fixture above is a git tree, so nothing
+# reached that arm. GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES stops git's upward search at $TMP, so the fixture is never inside a repo.
+F="$TMP/c9"; mkdir -p "$F/Blockchain/Dev/scripts"
+cp "$RUNNER" "$F/Blockchain/Dev/scripts/run-code-guards.sh"
+out9=$( cd "$F/Blockchain/Dev" && GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES="$TMP" bash scripts/run-code-guards.sh --check-unreached 2>&1; echo "rc=$?" )
+check "a non-git tree: the census exits 0" "rc=0" "$(printf '%s\n' "$out9" | tail -1)"
+check "a non-git tree: the census prints the advisory SKIP line" "yes" "$(printf '%s\n' "$out9" | grep -q '^SKIP (advisory)' && echo yes || echo no)"
 echo
```

## Cells

- `skip-rc` = `a non-git tree: the census exits 0`
- `skip-line` = `a non-git tree: the census prints the advisory SKIP line`

From:

To:


### MSG the advisory arm stops saying SKIP (advisory)
File: `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/run-code-guards.sh`
Line: 146
From:
```
    echo "SKIP (advisory) — not a git checkout, cannot enumerate tracked guards"
```
To:
```

```
Reds: `skip-line`

### ARM the non-git test is dropped (a non-git tree falls through to the census)
File: `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/run-code-guards.sh`
Line: 145
From:
```
  if ! command -v git >/dev/null 2>&1 || ! git -C "$REPO_ROOT" rev-parse --git-dir >/dev/null 2>&1; then
```
To:

Reds: `skip-rc`, `skip-line`

## Controls

- `census sees the orphan`

files.Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/run_cod:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# TESTS for run-code-guards.sh (KS-926)
# =============================================================================
# run-code-guards.sh exists because seventeen guards ran from no entry point —
# checks that could not fail. Shipping its census WITHOUT assertions would
# reproduce that defect one level up: a census that cannot fail is worth exactly
# as much as the guards it is meant to account for. So every case here asserts
# an EXIT CODE, which is what the preflight branches on.
#
# Each negative case carries a RED-PROOF that actually RUNS: the tampered copy is
# `bash -n`-checked before it is executed, because a tamper that breaks parsing
# reddens while executing zero of the logic under test — a green-looking red.
#
# Fixture is a REAL `git init` tree: the census enumerates via `git ls-files`, so
# without a git checkout it self-SKIPs and every verdict below is unreachable.
#
# bash 3.2 (macOS, and what the pre-push hook runs): no mapfile, no associative
# arrays, empty arrays expanded with the +alternate form.
#
# Usage: bash Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/run_code_guards.test.sh
# =============================================================================
set -uo pipefail

HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
RUNNER="${CODE_GUARDS_SH:-$HERE/../run-code-guards.sh}"
[ -f "$RUNNER" ] || { echo "FATAL: run-code-guards.sh not found at $RUNNER" >&2; exit 2; }

TMP="$(mktemp -d)"; trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT
PASS=0; FAIL=0
check() {
  if [ "$2" = "$3" ]; then echo "  ok   $1 (=$3)"; PASS=$((PASS+1))
  else echo "  FAIL $1 — expected $2, got $3"; FAIL=$((FAIL+1)); fi
}

# Build a fixture repo. $1 = dir. Creates a git tree with three guards, all of
# which exit 0, and a copy of the runner whose buckets name exactly those three.
make_fixture() {
  local root="$1"
  mkdir -p "$root/Blockchain/Dev/scripts"
  ( cd "$root" && git init -q . && git config user.email t@t && git config user.name t )
  local g
  for g in check-alpha check-beta check-gamma; do
    printf '#!/usr/bin/env bash\nexit 0\n' > "$root/Blockchain/Dev/scripts/$g.sh"
  done
  # The runner, with its three buckets rewritten to the fixture's guards.
  python3 - "$RUNNER" "$root/Blockchain/Dev/scripts/run-code-guards.sh" <<'PY'
import re,sys
src,dst=sys.argv[1],sys.argv[2]
s=open(src,encoding='utf-8').read()
s=re.sub(r'^WIRED=\(.*?^\)$', 'WIRED=(\n  check-alpha.sh\n  check-beta.sh\n)', s, flags=re.S|re.M)
s=re.sub(r'^HOMED_ELSEWHERE=\(.*?^\)$', 'HOMED_ELSEWHERE=(\n  "check-gamma.sh|fixture entry point"\n)', s, flags=re.S|re.M)
s=re.sub(r'^DEFERRED=\(.*?^\)$', 'DEFERRED=(\n)', s, flags=re.S|re.M)
open(dst,'w',encoding='utf-8').write(s)
PY
  ( cd "$root" && git add -A && git commit -qm fixture )
}

# Run a fixture's runner. $1 = root, $2.. = args. Echoes exit code.
run_fx() { local root="$1"; shift; ( cd "$root/Blockchain/Dev" && bash scripts/run-code-guards.sh "$@" >/dev/null 2>&1; echo $?; ); }

# A tamper must still PARSE, or its red proves nothing.
assert_parses() { bash -n "$1" 2>/dev/null || { echo "  FAIL tamper broke parsing: $1"; FAIL=$((FAIL+1)); return 1; }; }

echo "=== CASE 1 — a fully bucketed tree: census OK, guards run green ==="
F="$TMP/c1"; make_fixture "$F"
check "census on a clean fixture" 0 "$(run_fx "$F" --check-unreached)"
check "run of two green guards"   0 "$(run_fx "$F")"
check "--list"                    0 "$(run_fx "$F" --list)"

echo "=== CASE 2 — RED-PROOF: a tracked guard in NO bucket must fail the census ==="
F="$TMP/c2"; make_fixture "$F"
printf '#!/usr/bin/env bash\nexit 0\n' > "$F/Blockchain/Dev/scripts/check-orphan.sh"
( cd "$F" && git add -A && git commit -qm orphan )
check "census sees the orphan" 1 "$(run_fx "$F" --check-unreached)"
# and the same tree is otherwise fine, so the 1 is attributable to the orphan
check "control: run path unaffected by an unbucketed guard" 0 "$(run_fx "$F")"

echo "=== CASE 3 — RED-PROOF: a bucket naming a guard NOT in the tree must fail ==="
F="$TMP/c3"; make_fixture "$F"
R="$F/Blockchain/Dev/scripts/run-code-guards.sh"
sed -i.bak 's/^  check-beta\.sh$/  check-beta.sh\n  check-ghost.sh/' "$R" && rm -f "$R.bak"
if assert_parses "$R"; then
  check "census sees the ghost" 1 "$(run_fx "$F" --check-unreached)"
fi

echo "=== CASE 4 — POSITIVE CONTROL: enumerating ZERO guards must FAIL, not pass ==="
# This is the defect KS-926 is about, reproduced inside its own fix: if the
# pathspec stops matching, `comm` finds no orphans and the census would report a
# clean bill of health having examined nothing.
F="$TMP/c4"; make_fixture "$F"
R="$F/Blockchain/Dev/scripts/run-code-guards.sh"
sed -i.bak "s|ls-files 'Blockchain/Dev/scripts/check-\*.sh'|ls-files 'no/such/path/check-*.sh'|" "$R" && rm -f "$R.bak"
if assert_parses "$R"; then
  check "census with 0 tracked guards fails loudly" 1 "$(run_fx "$F" --check-unreached)"
fi

echo "=== CASE 5 — RED-PROOF: a wired guard that FAILS must fail the run ==="
F="$TMP/c5"; make_fixture "$F"
printf '#!/usr/bin/env bash\nexit 1\n' > "$F/Blockchain/Dev/scripts/check-beta.sh"
( cd "$F" && git add -A && git commit -qm redden )
check "run reports a red guard" 1 "$(run_fx "$F")"
check "control: census still OK (bucketing unchanged)" 0 "$(run_fx "$F" --check-unreached)"

echo "=== CASE 6 — POSITIVE CONTROL: running ZERO guards must FAIL, not pass ==="
F="$TMP/c6"; make_fixture "$F"
R="$F/Blockchain/Dev/scripts/run-code-guards.sh"
python3 - "$R" <<'PY'
import re,sys
p=sys.argv[1]; s=open(p,encoding='utf-8').read()
s=re.sub(r'^WIRED=\(.*?^\)$','WIRED=(\n)',s,flags=re.S|re.M)
open(p,'w',encoding='utf-8').write(s)
PY
if assert_parses "$R"; then
  check "run with an empty WIRED list fails loudly" 1 "$(run_fx "$F")"
fi

echo "=== CASE 7 — a wired guard missing from the tree must fail the run ==="
F="$TMP/c7"; make_fixture "$F"
( cd "$F" && git rm -q Blockchain/Dev/scripts/check-beta.sh && git commit -qm remove )
check "run reports a missing wired guard" 1 "$(run_fx "$F")"

echo "=== CASE 8 — the HOOK'S GIT ENV must not reach the guards (KS-926, found by wiring) ==="
# Git exports GIT_DIR to hooks. Under it, `rev-parse --show-toplevel` returns the
# directory asked from rather than the repo root, so guards resolve repo-root
# paths one level too deep and call present files MISSING. Measured on
# check-stack-safety.sh: exit 0 without GIT_DIR, exit 1 with it.
F="$TMP/c8"; make_fixture "$F"
# A guard that fails iff its repo root resolves wrongly — the defect, in miniature.
cat > "$F/Blockchain/Dev/scripts/check-alpha.sh" <<'GUARD'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
REPO="$(git -C "$ROOT" rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null || (cd "$ROOT/../.." && pwd))"
[ -f "$REPO/marker.txt" ] || { echo "::error::marker.txt missing (REPO=$REPO)"; exit 1; }
exit 0
GUARD
echo marker > "$F/marker.txt"
( cd "$F" && git add -A && git commit -qm hookenv )
GD="$(cd "$F" && git rev-parse --absolute-git-dir)"
# The guard alone, under the hook's env, must FAIL — otherwise this case proves nothing.
raw=$( cd "$F/Blockchain/Dev" && GIT_DIR="$GD" bash scripts/check-alpha.sh >/dev/null 2>&1; echo $? )
check "RED-PROOF: the guard alone under GIT_DIR does fail" 1 "$raw"
raw0=$( cd "$F/Blockchain/Dev" && bash scripts/check-alpha.sh >/dev/null 2>&1; echo $? )
check "control: the same guard without GIT_DIR passes" 0 "$raw0"
# Through the runner, which unsets it, the same guard must pass.
viarunner=$( cd "$F/Blockchain/Dev" && GIT_DIR="$GD" bash scripts/run-code-guards.sh >/dev/null 2>&1; echo $? )
check "the runner shields guards from the hook env" 0 "$viarunner"
# And removing the unset must bring the failure back — so the fix is load-bearing.
R="$F/Blockchain/Dev/scripts/run-code-guards.sh"
sed -i.bak 's/^unset GIT_DIR .*$/: # unset removed by the test/; s/^      GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY.*$/: # continuation removed/' "$R" && rm -f "$R.bak"
if assert_parses "$R"; then
  back=$( cd "$F/Blockchain/Dev" && GIT_DIR="$GD" bash scripts/run-code-guards.sh >/dev/null 2>&1; echo $? )
  check "RED-PROOF: removing the unset brings the failure back" 1 "$back"
fi

echo
echo "run_code_guards.test.sh — $PASS passed, $FAIL failed"
[ "$FAIL" -eq 0 ] || exit 1
